Continued public crypto activity while liquidators pursued recovery; Su Zhu was later jailed in Singapore for non-cooperation.

name: Chris Espinosa
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Apple Computer in 1976 at age 14 as employee number 8 while the company still operated from Steve Jobs's parents' garage, writing BASIC programs, documentation, and demonstrating the Apple I after school.
early_history_summary: Born September 18, 1961; attended Homestead High School (same school as Jobs and Wozniak). Met Jobs at the Byte Shop, befriended Wozniak via Homebrew Computer Club, and began after-school work at Apple in 1976. Briefly attended UC Berkeley with Andy Hertzfeld as freshman advisor before Jobs convinced him to drop out in 1981 to work full-time in publications and product software.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Silicon Valley near Cupertino/Los Altos. Mother worked at Stanford as head of single-student housing and had collaborated with the CS department on housing software, and sometimes drove him to Homebrew meetings.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother had operational exposure to Stanford computing/housing systems and later worked with word-processing sales/training; not a direct engineer parent, but provided access and transport into early personal-computer culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Apple employee #8, Homebrew, Homestead High, Silicon Valley, Jobs garage, teenage coding
evidence_summary: Espinosa became Apple employee #8 at 14 in 1976, embedding immediately in the personal-computer founding team. Geographic proximity to Jobs/Wozniak, early computer access, mother-enabled Homebrew attendance, and continuous product work through Mac OS, HyperCard, AppleScript, Xcode, and iOS Family Sharing produced one of the longest continuous engineering careers in tech. Advantages are primarily frontier geography, early specialization, and elite founder network rather than inherited capital.
starting_point: Born September 18, 1961, in Silicon Valley; Homestead High student whose mother worked at Stanford and facilitated early Homebrew Computer Club access.
current_position: Longest-serving Apple employee (employee #8); still a senior Apple engineer/speaker as of Apple's 50th anniversary coverage in 2026.

trajectory.event: Joined Apple as employee number 8, writing BASIC programs and demonstrating Apple I systems from Jobs's garage.
Dropped out of UC Berkeley at Jobs's urging to work full-time in Apple publications; received WozPlan pre-IPO share opportunity.
Contributed as part of the original Macintosh software/publications ecosystem around Mac launch.
Continued core platform work spanning classic Mac OS, A/UX, HyperCard, and related Apple software initiatives.
Served in AIM-alliance era roles including Taligent/Kaleida project management.
Publicly associated with iOS Family Sharing and ongoing Xcode/macOS platform work.
Profiled by The New York Times as Apple's longest-serving employee at the company's 50-year mark.
